chapters.title: Elijah and Ahaziah
chapters.html:
2 Kings 1

Ahaziah Inquires of Baal-zebub

1After the death of Ahab, Moab rebelled against Israel.

2Ahaziah fell through the lattice in his upper room in Samaria and was injured. So he sent messengers, telling them, "Go, inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, whether I shall recover from this injury."

3But the messenger of the LORD said to Elijah the Tishbite, "Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and say to them, 'Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron?

4Now therefore thus says the LORD: You shall not come down from the bed to which you have gone up, but you shall surely die.'" So Elijah went.

5The messengers returned to the king, and he said to them, "Why have you come back?"

6They said to him, "A man came up to meet us and said to us, 'Go back to the king who sent you, and say to him, "Thus says the LORD: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are sending to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron? Therefore you shall not come down from the bed to which you have gone up, but you shall surely die."'"

7He said to them, "What kind of man was he who came up to meet you and told you these things?"

8They answered him, "A hairy man, with a leather belt girded around his waist." He said, "It is Elijah the Tishbite."

Fire from Heaven

9Then the king sent to him a captain of fifty with his fifty men. He went up to him, and there he was, sitting on the top of the hill. He said to him, "Man of God, the king says, 'Come down!'"

10But Elijah answered the captain of fifty, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty." Then fire came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty.

11Again the king sent to him another captain of fifty with his fifty. He answered and said to him, "Man of God, thus says the king: 'Come down quickly!'"

12But Elijah answered them, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty." Then the fire of God came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty.

13Again the king sent the captain of a third fifty with his fifty. The third captain of fifty went up and came and fell on his knees before Elijah, and pleaded with him, "Man of God, please let my life and the life of these fifty servants of yours be precious in your sight.

14Fire has come down from heaven and consumed the two former captains of fifty with their fifties. But now let my life be precious in your sight."

15Then the messenger of the LORD said to Elijah, "Go down with him; do not be afraid of him." So he arose and went down with him to the king,

16and said to him, "Thus says the LORD: 'Because you have sent messengers to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron — is it because there is no God in Israel to inquire of His word? — therefore you shall not come down from the bed to which you have gone up, but you shall surely die.'"

17So he died according to the word of the LORD that Elijah had spoken. Jehoram reigned in his place, in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, because he had no son.

18The rest of the acts of Ahaziah that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

Notes

  • v2 "Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron" — Ba'al Zevuv, lord of flies, the god of a Philistine city. In the Gospels the Pharisees say Jesus casts out demons by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons (Matthew 12:24).

  • vv2–3 "he sent messengers… the messenger of the LORD said to Elijah… to meet the messengers of the king" — mal'akhim and mal'akh YHWH, the same word for the king's envoys and the LORD's. The king sends his to Ekron; the LORD sends His to stop them.

  • vv3, 6, 16 "Is it because there is no God in Israel" — ha-mibbeli ein Elohim be-Yisra'el, asked three times, each time with the same sentence of death after it.

  • vv4, 6, 16 "You shall not come down from the bed to which you have gone up" — alita… lo tered: the king has gone up to his bed and will not come down; Elijah on the hill is told to come down (vv9, 11), and goes down only at the LORD's word (v15).

  • v8 "A hairy man, with a leather belt girded around his waist" — ish ba'al se'ar, a man of hair. Elijah's garment is his adderet, cloak (1 Kings 19:13, 19), and Zechariah speaks of the prophets' adderet se'ar, hairy cloak (Zechariah 13:4). John the Baptist wore clothing of camel's hair and a leather belt around his waist (Matthew 3:4).

  • vv10, 12 "If I am a man of God, let fire come down" — ish and esh, man and fire, near in sound. When a Samaritan village would not receive Jesus, James and John asked, Lord, do you want us to bid fire come down from heaven and consume them? (Luke 9:54).

  • v13 "please let my life… be precious in your sight" — the third captain asks instead of commanding, and lives.

  • v15 "the messenger of the LORD said to Elijah… do not be afraid of him" — the prophet goes to the king who sought him, at the LORD's word.

  • v17 "Jehoram reigned in his place, in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat" — two kings named Jehoram, one in Israel and one in Judah. Later the text puts Jehoram of Israel's accession in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat (3:1); both dates stand in the text. Because he had no son: his brother succeeded him.

chapters.title: Elijah Taken Up
chapters.html:
2 Kings 2

From Gilgal to the Jordan

1And it came to pass, when the LORD was about to take Elijah up to heaven in a whirlwind, that Elijah and Elisha were going from Gilgal.

2Elijah said to Elisha, "Please stay here, for the LORD has sent me as far as Bethel." But Elisha said, "As the LORD lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." So they went down to Bethel.

3The sons of the prophets who were at Bethel came out to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today the LORD will take your master from over your head?" He said, "Yes, I know it; keep silent."

4Elijah said to him, "Elisha, please stay here, for the LORD has sent me to Jericho." But he said, "As the LORD lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." So they came to Jericho.

5The sons of the prophets who were at Jericho came near to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today the LORD will take your master from over your head?" He answered, "Yes, I know it; keep silent."

6Then Elijah said to him, "Please stay here, for the LORD has sent me to the Jordan." But he said, "As the LORD lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." So the two of them went on.

7Fifty men of the sons of the prophets went and stood at a distance facing them, while the two of them stood by the Jordan.

8Then Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up and struck the water, and the water was divided to one side and to the other, so that the two of them crossed over on dry ground.

The Chariot of Fire

9And it came to pass, when they had crossed, that Elijah said to Elisha, "Ask what I shall do for you before I am taken from you." Elisha said, "Please let a double portion of your spirit be on me."

10He said, "You have asked a hard thing. If you see me as I am being taken from you, it shall be so for you; but if not, it shall not be so."

11And it came to pass, as they were still going on and talking, that a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated the two of them, and Elijah went up in a whirlwind to heaven.

12Elisha saw it and cried out, "My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!" He saw him no more. Then he took hold of his own clothes and tore them in two pieces.

13He took up the cloak of Elijah that had fallen from him, and went back and stood on the bank of the Jordan.

14He took the cloak of Elijah that had fallen from him and struck the water and said, "Where is the LORD, the God of Elijah?" When he too had struck the water, it was divided to one side and to the other, and Elisha crossed over.

Elisha at Jericho

15When the sons of the prophets who were at Jericho saw him from a distance, they said, "The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha." They came to meet him and bowed down to the ground before him.

16They said to him, "Your servants have with them fifty strong men. Please let them go and look for your master. It may be that the Spirit of the LORD has taken him up and cast him on some mountain or into some valley." He said, "You shall not send them."

17But when they urged him until he was ashamed, he said, "Send them." So they sent fifty men, and they searched for three days but did not find him.

18They came back to him while he was staying at Jericho, and he said to them, "Did I not say to you, 'Do not go'?"

19The men of the city said to Elisha, "The situation of this city is pleasant, as my lord sees, but the water is bad and the land causes miscarriage."

20He said, "Bring me a new bowl, and put salt in it." So they brought it to him.

21Then he went to the spring of water and threw salt in it and said, "Thus says the LORD: 'I have healed this water; from now on neither death nor miscarriage shall come from it.'"

22So the water has been healed to this day, according to the word that Elisha spoke.

The Boys of Bethel

23He went up from there to Bethel. As he was going up on the way, some small boys came out of the city and mocked him, saying to him, "Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!"

24He turned around, looked at them and cursed them in the name of the LORD. Then two she-bears came out of the woods and tore forty-two of the boys.

25From there he went to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.

Notes

  • vv2, 4, 6 "As the LORD lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you" — three times Elijah tells Elisha to stay, and three times Elisha swears the same oath. At Bethel and Jericho the sons of the prophets ask him the same question, and he gives the same answer.

  • v3 "the LORD will take your master from over your head" — me-al roshekha, from over your head, from his place above you.

  • vv8, 14 "struck the water… crossed over on dry ground" — ba-charavah, the word of the crossing of the sea, the sons of Israel came into the middle of the sea on dry ground (Exodus 14:22), and of the Jordan under Joshua (Joshua 3:17). Elijah crosses east as Joshua crossed west; Elisha comes back across as Joshua did.

  • v9 "a double portion of your spirit" — pi shenayim, the firstborn's share of an inheritance, a double portion of all that he has (Deuteronomy 21:17). Elisha asks to be Elijah's heir, not to be twice Elijah.

  • v11 "a chariot of fire and horses of fire… Elijah went up in a whirlwind to heaven" — bi-se'arah, in a storm wind. The text says the chariot came between them; it was the whirlwind that carried Elijah up.

  • v12 "My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!" — the same cry King Joash will raise at Elisha's deathbed (13:14).

  • vv15–16 "The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha… the Spirit of the LORD has taken him up" — Elijah's own spirit, lowercase; ruach YHWH, capital, as fixed. The sons of the prophets feared the Spirit might carry Elijah off, as Obadiah had (1 Kings 18:12).

  • vv19–22 "the land causes miscarriage… neither death nor miscarriage" — meshakkelet, from shakhal, to be bereaved of children. Salt in a new bowl, and the word I have healed.

  • v23 "some small boys… Go up, baldhead!" — ne'arim qetannim; in v24 they are yeladim, children or youths. Go up, aleh, is the verb of Elijah's going up (vv1, 11).

  • v24 "two she-bears… tore forty-two of the boys" — va-tevaqqa'nah, tore open. The text does not say that the boys died.

chapters.title: The War against Moab
chapters.html:
2 Kings 3

Jehoram King of Israel

1Jehoram son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned twelve years.

2He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, though not like his father and his mother, for he removed the pillar of Baal that his father had made.

3Nevertheless he clung to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, with which he made Israel to sin; he did not turn away from them.

Three Kings against Moab

4Now Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder, and he used to pay the king of Israel a hundred thousand lambs and the wool of a hundred thousand rams.

5But when Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.

6So King Jehoram went out of Samaria at that time and mustered all Israel.

7He went and sent word to Jehoshaphat king of Judah: "The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me to battle against Moab?" He said, "I will go up. I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses."

8He said, "Which way shall we go up?" He answered, "By the way of the wilderness of Edom."

9So the king of Israel went with the king of Judah and the king of Edom. When they had made a circuit of seven days' journey, there was no water for the army or for the animals that followed them.

10Then the king of Israel said, "Alas! The LORD has called these three kings to give them into the hand of Moab."

11But Jehoshaphat said, "Is there no prophet of the LORD here, through whom we may inquire of the LORD?" One of the servants of the king of Israel answered, "Elisha son of Shaphat is here, who poured water on the hands of Elijah."

12Jehoshaphat said, "The word of the LORD is with him." So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom went down to him.

Elisha's Word

13Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What have I to do with you? Go to the prophets of your father and the prophets of your mother." But the king of Israel said to him, "No, for the LORD has called these three kings to give them into the hand of Moab."

14Elisha said, "As the LORD of hosts lives, before whom I stand, were it not that I have regard for Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would neither look at you nor see you.

15But now bring me a musician." When the musician played, the hand of the LORD came on him.

16He said, "Thus says the LORD: 'Make this valley full of pits.'

17For thus says the LORD: 'You shall not see wind or see rain, yet that valley shall be filled with water, so that you shall drink, you and your cattle and your animals.'

18This is a light thing in the eyes of the LORD; He will also give Moab into your hand.

19You shall strike every fortified city and every choice city, and fell every good tree, and stop up all springs of water, and ruin every good piece of land with stones."

20And it came to pass in the morning, about the time of offering the grain offering, that water came from the direction of Edom, and the country was filled with water.

The Water Red as Blood

21When all the Moabites heard that the kings had come up to fight against them, all who were able to put on armor, from the youngest up, were called out, and they stood at the border.

22They rose early in the morning, and the sun shone on the water, and the Moabites saw the water opposite them as red as blood.

23They said, "This is blood! The kings have surely fought together and struck one another down. Now then, Moab, to the spoil!"

24But when they came to the camp of Israel, the Israelites rose up and struck the Moabites, so that they fled before them. They went forward, striking the Moabites as they went.

25They overthrew the cities, and on every good piece of land each man threw a stone until they filled it. They stopped up every spring of water and felled every good tree, until only the stones of Kir-hareseth were left, and the slingers surrounded it and struck it.

26When the king of Moab saw that the battle was going against him, he took with him seven hundred men who drew the sword, to break through to the king of Edom, but they could not.

27Then he took his firstborn son, who was to reign in his place, and offered him as a burnt offering on the wall. Then there came great wrath against Israel, and they withdrew from him and returned to their own land.

Notes

  • v2 "he removed the pillar of Baal that his father had made" — matstsevet ha-Ba'al. Later Jehu will break the pillar of Baal again and tear down its house (10:27).

  • v4 "Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder" — noqed, the word Amos uses of himself, who was among the sheep breeders of Tekoa (Amos 1:1). The tribute is counted in lambs and wool.

  • v7 "I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses" — the words Jehoshaphat said to Ahab before Ramoth-gilead (1 Kings 22:4).

  • v11 "who poured water on the hands of Elijah" — the servant's task. Elisha is known by his service to his master.

  • v13 "Go to the prophets of your father and the prophets of your mother" — the prophets of Baal and Asherah who ate at Jezebel's table (1 Kings 18:19). Mah li va-lakh, as in 1 Kings 17:18.

  • v15 "bring me a musician" — menaggen. As the musician plays, the hand of the LORD came on him, the phrase used of Elijah before he ran to Jezreel (1 Kings 18:46).

  • vv19, 25 "fell every good tree… felled every good tree" — the law of siege says, you shall not destroy its trees by swinging an axe against them… you shall not cut them down (Deuteronomy 20:19). Here the prophet's word commands it against Moab, and it is done.

  • vv20–22 "water came from the direction of Edom… the water… as red as blood" — adummim ka-dam, red as blood; adom, red, and Edom are the same letters. The water comes mi-derekh Edom, and the Moabites see it adom.

  • v25 "until only the stones of Kir-hareseth were left" — the capital of Moab, the last city standing.

  • v27 "offered him as a burnt offering on the wall. Then there came great wrath against Israel" — qetsef gadol. Whose wrath is not said: God's, Moab's, or the other kings'. The Greek has great remorse. The text keeps the Hebrew.

chapters.title: Elisha, the Widow and the Shunammite
chapters.html:
2 Kings 4

The Widow's Oil

1A certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, "Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that your servant feared the LORD. Now the creditor has come to take my two children to be his slaves."

2Elisha said to her, "What shall I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?" She said, "Your servant has nothing in the house except a jar of oil."

3He said, "Go outside, borrow vessels from all your neighbors, empty vessels, and not too few.

4Then go in and shut the door behind you and your sons, and pour into all these vessels. As each is filled, set it aside."

5So she went from him and shut the door behind her and her sons. They kept bringing vessels to her, and she kept pouring.

6And it came to pass, when the vessels were full, that she said to her son, "Bring me another vessel." He said to her, "There is not another vessel." Then the oil stopped.

7She came and told the man of God, and he said, "Go, sell the oil and pay your debt, and you and your sons can live on the rest."

The Shunammite Woman

8And it came to pass one day that Elisha passed through Shunem, where a wealthy woman lived, and she urged him to eat bread. So whenever he passed that way, he would turn in there to eat bread.

9She said to her husband, "I know now that this is a holy man of God who is continually passing our way.

10Let us make a small room with walls on the roof, and put a bed there for him, a table, a chair and a lamp. And it shall come to pass, whenever he comes to us, that he can turn in there."

11And it came to pass one day that he came there, and he turned into the upper room and lay down there.

12He said to Gehazi his servant, "Call this Shunammite." When he had called her, she stood before him.

13He said to him, "Say now to her, 'You have taken all this trouble for us. What can be done for you? Would you have a word spoken for you to the king or to the commander of the army?'" She answered, "I live among my own people."

14He said, "What then can be done for her?" Gehazi answered, "Well, she has no son, and her husband is old."

15He said, "Call her." When he had called her, she stood in the doorway.

16He said, "At this appointed time, at the time of life, you shall embrace a son." She said, "No, my lord, man of God, do not lie to your servant."

17But the woman conceived and bore a son at that appointed time, at the time of life, as Elisha had said to her.

The Shunammite's Son

18When the child had grown, it came to pass one day that he went out to his father among the reapers.

19He said to his father, "My head, my head!" The father said to his servant, "Carry him to his mother."

20When he had lifted him up and brought him to his mother, the child sat on her knees until noon, and then he died.

21She went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, shut the door behind him and went out.

22Then she called to her husband and said, "Please send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, so that I may hurry to the man of God and come back."

23He said, "Why are you going to him today? It is neither new moon nor sabbath." She said, "It is well."

24Then she saddled the donkey and said to her servant, "Drive on; do not slow the pace for me unless I tell you."

25So she set out and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. And it came to pass, when the man of God saw her at a distance, that he said to Gehazi his servant, "There is the Shunammite.

26Run now to meet her and say to her, 'Is it well with you? Is it well with your husband? Is it well with the child?'" She answered, "It is well."

27When she came to the man of God on the mountain, she took hold of his feet. Gehazi came near to push her away, but the man of God said, "Let her alone, for her soul is bitter within her, and the LORD has hidden it from me and has not told me."

28She said, "Did I ask my lord for a son? Did I not say, 'Do not deceive me'?"

29He said to Gehazi, "Gird up your loins, take my staff in your hand and go. If you meet anyone, do not greet him, and if anyone greets you, do not answer him. Lay my staff on the face of the child."

30Then the mother of the child said, "As the LORD lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." So he got up and followed her.

31Gehazi went on ahead of them and laid the staff on the face of the child, but there was no voice and no response. So he went back to meet him and told him, "The child has not awakened."

32When Elisha came into the house, the child was dead, laid on his bed.

33So he went in and shut the door behind the two of them and prayed to the LORD.

34Then he went up and lay on the child, putting his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes and his hands on his hands. As he stretched himself out on him, the flesh of the child became warm.

35Then he got up and walked once back and forth in the house, and went up and stretched himself out on him. The child sneezed seven times, and the child opened his eyes.

36He called Gehazi and said, "Call this Shunammite." So he called her, and when she came to him, he said, "Pick up your son."

37She came and fell at his feet, bowing to the ground. Then she picked up her son and went out.

Death in the Pot

38Elisha came back to Gilgal when there was a famine in the land. As the sons of the prophets were sitting before him, he said to his servant, "Set on the large pot and boil stew for the sons of the prophets."

39One of them went out into the field to gather herbs, and found a wild vine and gathered from it wild gourds, his lap full, and came and cut them up into the pot of stew, for they did not know what they were.

40They poured it out for the men to eat. And it came to pass, as they were eating of the stew, that they cried out, "There is death in the pot, man of God!" And they could not eat it.

41He said, "Then bring flour." He threw it into the pot and said, "Pour it out for the people, so that they may eat." There was no harm in the pot.

Bread for a Hundred Men

42A man came from Baal-shalishah and brought the man of God bread of the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley, and fresh ears of grain in his sack. He said, "Give to the people, so that they may eat."

43But his servant said, "How can I set this before a hundred men?" He said, "Give to the people, so that they may eat, for thus says the LORD: 'They shall eat and have some left.'"

44So he set it before them, and they ate and had some left, according to the word of the LORD.

Notes

  • v1 "the creditor has come to take my two children to be his slaves" — the law allowed a poor Israelite to be sold to work off debt, but you shall not make him work as a slave works (Leviticus 25:39).

  • vv4–6 "shut the door… Then the oil stopped" — the oil runs as long as there are vessels to hold it, as the jar of flour and jug of oil held out for the widow of Zarephath (1 Kings 17:14–16).

  • v8 "a wealthy woman" — ishah gedolah, a great woman: of standing and means.

  • vv16–17 "At this appointed time, at the time of life, you shall embrace a son" — la-mo'ed ha-zeh ka-et chayyah, the words the LORD spoke to Abraham about Sarah, At the appointed time I will return to you, at the time of life, and Sarah shall have a son (Genesis 18:14).

  • v23 "It is neither new moon nor sabbath… It is well" — her husband's question implies that those were the days to visit a man of God. Shalom, she says, to her husband and again to Gehazi (v26), and tells the truth only at Elisha's feet.

  • v29 "If you meet anyone, do not greet him" — Jesus gave the same charge to those He sent out: greet no one on the road (Luke 10:4).

  • v30 "As the LORD lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you" — Elisha's own oath to Elijah (2:2, 4, 6), now spoken to him.

  • vv34–35 "his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes and his hands on his hands" — as Elijah stretched himself out on the widow's son at Zarephath (1 Kings 17:21). The staff laid on the child's face did nothing (v31). Va-yizorer, sneezed, is found only here.

  • vv39–41 "wild gourds… There is death in the pot" — paqqu'ot sadeh, from the root of the carved gourds of the temple (1 Kings 6:18). Flour is thrown in, and the danger is gone.

  • vv42–44 "twenty loaves of barley… They shall eat and have some left" — akhol ve-hoter. In the Gospel of John a boy has five barley loaves and two fish, and after the crowd eats, they filled twelve baskets with fragments from the five barley loaves (John 6:9, 13).

chapters.title: Naaman Healed
chapters.html:
2 Kings 5

The Girl from Israel

1Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a great man before his master and highly regarded, because by him the LORD had given victory to Aram. The man was a mighty man of valor, but he had blight.

2Now the Arameans had gone out on raids and had taken captive from the land of Israel a little girl, and she served Naaman's wife.

3She said to her mistress, "If only my lord were with the prophet who is in Samaria! Then he would take away his blight."

4So Naaman went in and told his lord, "Thus and thus spoke the girl from the land of Israel."

5The king of Aram said, "Go now, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel." So he went, taking with him ten talents of silver, six thousand shekels of gold and ten changes of clothes.

6He brought the letter to the king of Israel, which said, "Now when this letter comes to you, know that I have sent Naaman my servant to you, so that you may take away his blight."

7And it came to pass, when the king of Israel read the letter, that he tore his clothes and said, "Am I God, to put to death and to make alive, that this man sends word to me to take away a man's blight? Only consider, and see how he is seeking a quarrel with me."

Wash in the Jordan

8And it came to pass, when Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, that he sent to the king, saying, "Why have you torn your clothes? Let him come to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel."

9So Naaman came with his horses and his chariots and stood at the door of Elisha's house.

10Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, "Go and wash in the Jordan seven times, and your flesh shall be restored to you, and you shall be clean."

11But Naaman was angry and went away and said, "I thought that he would surely come out to me and stand and call on the name of the LORD his God, and wave his hand over the place and take away the blight.

12Are not Abana and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not wash in them and be clean?" So he turned and went away in a rage.

13But his servants came near and spoke to him and said, "My father, if the prophet had told you to do some great thing, would you not have done it? How much more, then, when he says to you, 'Wash, and be clean'?"

14So he went down and dipped himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the word of the man of God, and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.

Naaman's Confession

15Then he returned to the man of God, he and all his company, and he came and stood before him and said, "Now I know that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel. So now please accept a gift from your servant."

16But he said, "As the LORD lives, before whom I stand, I will accept nothing." He urged him to accept it, but he refused.

17Then Naaman said, "If not, please let your servant be given two mules' load of earth, for your servant will no longer offer burnt offering or sacrifice to other gods, but only to the LORD.

18In this matter may the LORD pardon your servant: when my master goes into the house of Rimmon to bow down there, leaning on my arm, and I bow down in the house of Rimmon — when I bow down in the house of Rimmon, may the LORD pardon your servant in this matter."

19He said to him, "Go in peace." So he went from him some distance.

Gehazi

20Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said, "My master has spared this Naaman the Aramean, in not accepting from his hand what he brought. As the LORD lives, I will run after him and take something from him."

21So Gehazi pursued Naaman. When Naaman saw someone running after him, he got down from the chariot to meet him and said, "Is all well?"

22He said, "All is well. My master has sent me, saying, 'Just now two young men of the sons of the prophets have come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Please give them a talent of silver and two changes of clothes.'"

23Naaman said, "Be pleased to accept two talents." He urged him, and tied up two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of clothes, and gave them to two of his servants, and they carried them before him.

24When he came to the hill, he took them from their hand and stored them in the house, and he sent the men away, and they left.

25He went in and stood before his master, and Elisha said to him, "Where have you been, Gehazi?" He said, "Your servant has not gone anywhere."

26But he said to him, "Did not my heart go with you when a man turned from his chariot to meet you? Is it a time to accept silver and to accept clothes, olive groves and vineyards, sheep and oxen, male servants and female servants?

27Therefore the blight of Naaman shall cling to you and to your seed forever." So he went out from his presence with blight, white as snow.

Notes

  • v1 "a mighty man of valor, but he had blight" — gibbor chayil metsora: the sentence builds his greatness and ends on one word. Tsara'at is fixed as blight. By him the LORD had given victory to Aram: the God of Israel gave the Aramean his victories.

  • vv2, 14 "a little girl… like the flesh of a little child" — na'arah qetannah and na'ar qatan. The captive girl sets it in motion, and Naaman's flesh comes back like a small boy's.

  • v7 "Am I God, to put to death and to make alive?" — the words of the Song of Moses, I put to death and I make alive (Deuteronomy 32:39).

  • vv10, 14 "wash in the Jordan seven times… and you shall be clean" — the law's cleansing from blight was done seven times (Leviticus 14:7). The prophet does not come out; he sends a messenger.

  • v12 "Abana and Pharpar" — the written text has Avanah, the read form Amanah; the text keeps the familiar name Abana, which the Greek also has.

  • v15 "there is no God in all the earth except in Israel" — a foreign commander says it after seven dips in Israel's river. Jesus names him: there were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, and none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian (Luke 4:27).

  • v17 "two mules' load of earth" — soil of the land of Israel, to worship the LORD on in Aram.

  • v18 "the house of Rimmon… may the LORD pardon your servant" — Rimmon, the god of Damascus. Naaman asks in advance for pardon for bowing when his duty requires it; Elisha answers only Go in peace.

  • vv20–26 "As the LORD lives, I will run after him… Did not my heart go with you" — Gehazi takes the oath his master used to refuse the gift (v16) to go and get it. Olive groves and vineyards, sheep and oxen: the things the silver would buy.

  • v27 "with blight, white as snow" — as Miriam was blighted, white as snow (Numbers 12:10), and Moses' hand (Exodus 4:6).

chapters.title: The Floating Axe Head and the Siege of Samaria
chapters.html:
2 Kings 6

The Axe Head

1The sons of the prophets said to Elisha, "The place where we live under your charge is too cramped for us.

2Let us go to the Jordan, and each of us take a beam from there, and let us make a place there for us to live." He said, "Go."

3Then one of them said, "Please be willing to go with your servants." He answered, "I will go."

4So he went with them. When they came to the Jordan, they cut down trees.

5But as one of them was felling a beam, the iron head fell into the water. He cried out and said, "Alas, my lord! It was borrowed."

6The man of God said, "Where did it fall?" When he showed him the place, he cut off a stick and threw it in there, and made the iron float.

7He said, "Pick it up." So he reached out his hand and took it.

Horses and Chariots of Fire

8Now the king of Aram was at war with Israel. He took counsel with his servants, saying, "At such and such a place shall be my camp."

9But the man of God sent word to the king of Israel, "Beware of passing that place, for the Arameans are going down there."

10So the king of Israel sent to the place that the man of God told him. He warned him about it, and he was on his guard there, not once or twice.

11The heart of the king of Aram was greatly troubled by this. He called his servants and said to them, "Will you not tell me which of us is for the king of Israel?"

12One of his servants said, "No one, my lord the king. But Elisha, the prophet who is in Israel, tells the king of Israel the words that you speak in your bedroom."

13He said, "Go and see where he is, so that I may send and seize him." It was told him, "He is in Dothan."

14So he sent there horses and chariots and a great army. They came by night and surrounded the city.

15When the servant of the man of God rose early and went out, an army with horses and chariots was surrounding the city. His servant said to him, "Alas, my lord! What shall we do?"

16He said, "Do not be afraid, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them."

17Then Elisha prayed and said, "O LORD, please open his eyes, so that he may see." So the LORD opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw: the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.

18When the Arameans came down against him, Elisha prayed to the LORD and said, "Strike this people with blindness." So He struck them with blindness, according to the word of Elisha.

19Elisha said to them, "This is not the way, and this is not the city. Follow me, and I will bring you to the man you are seeking." So he led them to Samaria.

20And it came to pass, as soon as they came into Samaria, that Elisha said, "O LORD, open the eyes of these men, so that they may see." So the LORD opened their eyes, and they saw that they were in the middle of Samaria.

21When the king of Israel saw them, he said to Elisha, "My father, shall I strike them? Shall I strike them?"

22He answered, "You shall not strike them. Would you strike those whom you have taken captive with your sword and with your bow? Set bread and water before them, so that they may eat and drink and go to their master."

23So he prepared a great feast for them, and they ate and drank; then he sent them away, and they went to their master. The raiding bands of Aram did not come again into the land of Israel.

The Famine in Samaria

24And it came to pass after this that Ben-hadad king of Aram mustered all his army and went up and besieged Samaria.

25There was a great famine in Samaria as they besieged it, until a donkey's head was sold for eighty shekels of silver, and a quarter of a kab of dove's dung for five shekels of silver.

26And it came to pass, as the king of Israel was passing by on the wall, that a woman cried out to him, "Help, my lord the king!"

27He said, "If the LORD does not help you, how shall I help you? From the threshing floor, or from the winepress?"

28Then the king said to her, "What is troubling you?" She answered, "This woman said to me, 'Give your son, so that we may eat him today, and we will eat my son tomorrow.'

29So we boiled my son and ate him. On the next day I said to her, 'Give your son, so that we may eat him,' but she has hidden her son."

30And it came to pass, when the king heard the words of the woman, that he tore his clothes. He was passing by on the wall, and the people looked, and there was sackcloth underneath, on his flesh.

31He said, "So may God do to me, and more also, if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat remains on him today."

32Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. The king had sent a man ahead of him, but before the messenger came to him, Elisha said to the elders, "Do you see how this son of a murderer has sent to take off my head? Look, when the messenger comes, shut the door and hold the door fast against him. Is not the sound of his master's feet behind him?"

33While he was still speaking with them, the messenger came down to him and said, "This evil is from the LORD! Why should I wait for the LORD any longer?"

Notes

  • v5 "It was borrowed" — ve-hu sha'ul, and it was borrowed: the loss would fall on the borrower.

  • v8 "At such and such a place" — peloni almoni, the phrase Boaz uses for the unnamed kinsman in Ruth 4:1; here the king's plans are kept vague in the telling.

  • vv12, 17 "the words that you speak in your bedroom… he saw" — the prophet who hears the king's private words asks that his servant may see. The chapter turns on eyes: opened (v17), struck blind (v18), opened again in Samaria (v20).

  • v13 "He is in Dothan" — the place where Joseph found his brothers (Genesis 37:17).

  • v17 "horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha" — the chariot of fire that took Elijah (2:11), and the words Elisha cried then, the chariots of Israel and its horsemen (2:12).

  • v18 "Strike this people with blindness" — ba-sanverim, the word used of the men of Sodom at Lot's door, rendered in Genesis blindings (Genesis 19:11), and found only in these two places.

  • vv21–22 "My father, shall I strike them?… Set bread and water before them" — the king of Israel calls the prophet my father, as Elisha called Elijah (2:12). The prisoners are fed and sent home, and the raids stop (v23).

  • v25 "a donkey's head… a quarter of a kab of dove's dung" — food no one would eat, sold at a high price. The written text has chorei yonim, dove's dung; the read form is divyonim, another word for the same thing. The Greek has fifty shekels for the head.

  • vv28–29 "So we boiled my son and ate him" — the curse of the covenant: You will eat the fruit of your womb, the flesh of your sons and your daughters… in the siege (Deuteronomy 28:53).

  • vv32–33 "the messenger came down to him and said, 'This evil is from the LORD!'" — ha-mal'akh, the messenger. Ha-melekh, the king, differs by one letter, and in the next verse it is the king's officer who answers Elisha (7:2). The Hebrew and the Greek both have messenger, and the text keeps it.

speech.text: 2 Kings 6
The Axe Head
The sons of the prophets said to Elisha, "The place where we live under your charge is too cramped for us.
Let us go to the Jordan, and each of us take a beam from there, and let us make a place there for us to live." He said, "Go."
Then one of them said, "Please be willing to go with your servants." He answered, "I will go."
So he went with them. When they came to the Jordan, they cut down trees.
But as one of them was felling a beam, the iron head fell into the water. He cried out and said, "Alas, my lord! It was borrowed."
The man of God said, "Where did it fall?" When he showed him the place, he cut off a stick and threw it in there, and made the iron float.
He said, "Pick it up." So he reached out his hand and took it.
Horses and Chariots of Fire
Now the king of Aram was at war with Israel. He took counsel with his servants, saying, "At such and such a place shall be my camp."
But the man of God sent word to the king of Israel, "Beware of passing that place, for the Arameans are going down there."
So the king of Israel sent to the place that the man of God told him. He warned him about it, and he was on his guard there, not once or twice.
The heart of the king of Aram was greatly troubled by this. He called his servants and said to them, "Will you not tell me which of us is for the king of Israel?"
One of his servants said, "No one, my lord the king. But Elisha, the prophet who is in Israel, tells the king of Israel the words that you speak in your bedroom."
He said, "Go and see where he is, so that I may send and seize him." It was told him, "He is in Dothan."
So he sent there horses and chariots and a great army. They came by night and surrounded the city.
When the servant of the man of God rose early and went out, an army with horses and chariots was surrounding the city. His servant said to him, "Alas, my lord! What shall we do?"
He said, "Do not be afraid, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them."

Then Elisha prayed and said, "O LORD, please open his eyes, so that he may see." So the LORD opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw: the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
When the Arameans came down against him, Elisha prayed to the LORD and said, "Strike this people with blindness." So He struck them with blindness, according to the word of Elisha.
Elisha said to them, "This is not the way, and this is not the city. Follow me, and I will bring you to the man you are seeking." So he led them to Samaria.

And it came to pass, as soon as they came into Samaria, that Elisha said, "O LORD, open the eyes of these men, so that they may see." So the LORD opened their eyes, and they saw that they were in the middle of Samaria.
When the king of Israel saw them, he said to Elisha, "My father, shall I strike them? Shall I strike them?"

He answered, "You shall not strike them. Would you strike those whom you have taken captive with your sword and with your bow? Set bread and water before them, so that they may eat and drink and go to their master."
So he prepared a great feast for them, and they ate and drank; then he sent them away, and they went to their master. The raiding bands of Aram did not come again into the land of Israel.
